purpose: Static response routing and a controlled native WURM2 contact probe for the ten normal-enemy families.

shared_gate.guard: Each normal callback's contact tail first requires DS:8806 != 0.
shared_gate.player_coordinates: The selected pair is DS:87DE/DS:87E0 plus object+0x30*4; the callback compares those integer coordinates against family-specific object bounds.

01F7:4AB3.response_lifetime: 4C5D increments object+0x2A and clears object+0x18 after 0x28 ticks.
01F7:4AB3.effect_creation: Calls 01F7:4C8B for the contact response objects; the setup selects table DS:3344.

01F7:4BA0.response_lifetime: 4C5D increments object+0x2A and clears object+0x18 after 0x28 ticks.
01F7:4BA0.effect_creation: Calls 01F7:4EC9 for the contact response objects; the setup selects table DS:334E.

shared_gate.death_drop_conclusion: The player-contact branches redirect the enemy object to a timed response callback; they do not clear the enemy object or dispatch a drop. Normal-enemy object removal remains the shared camera/visibility path 01F7:1DCA -> 01F7:1DEE, which clears object+0x18 and the ARE record high byte at FS:[object+0x1A+1].

authored_lifecycle.stream_scan: 01F7:1CDA tracks 64-pixel camera regions and calls 01F7:1E04 for each loaded ARE declaration buffer.
authored_lifecycle.record_guard: 01F7:1E04 treats the low byte of each record word as the type; a high byte of 1 skips the record, while a first visit sets that high byte to 1 before creating the object and stores the record pointer at object+0x1A.
authored_lifecycle.removal_reset: 01F7:1DEE clears object+0x18 and writes zero to FS:[object+0x1A+1], undoing the streamed-record claimed mark.
authored_lifecycle.respawn_trigger: After an off-camera removal, 1DEE clears the source ARE claim. A same-level camera/cache sweep over the already-loaded region did not revisit the target at 1E04, while a full native level reload reread the ARE resource and recreated the family object. The 4AB3/4BA0 contact-response timeout clears only object+0x18 through 4C5D and is not an enemy death/drop path.

families.interaction: WURM2 contact selects the 4AB3/4C5D response after the x/y range gate.
BIENE contact selects the shared 4AB3/4C5D response.
FISCH contact selects the alternate 4BA0/4C5D response.
KRABBE contact selects the alternate 4BA0/4C5D response.
SCHNEE has camera/MAP and timer callbacks but no DS:8806 player-contact tail or 4AB3/4BA0 response write in 66E1/6757.
BUGGY contact paths converge on the 4AB3/4C5D response; one path publishes action word 13 before the callback switch.
UFO enemy contact publishes action word 13 on the first response phase and then switches to 4AB3/4C5D.

samples.note: Controlled gate reaches the WURM2 response switch; action is written by 4AB3 on the next callback.

conclusions: Seven normal-enemy families route player contact through the action-13 4AB3/4C5D response; FISCH and KRABBE use action 2 through 4BA0/4C5D.
SCHNEE has no equivalent player-contact response branch in its callback pair.
The response is a timed hit/effect state, not an enemy death or drop path; per-level respawn is therefore a reset/streaming question rather than a missing enemy callback transition.
